messages.subject: Detection History, "out dir" argument
parts:
Hello,
I would like to know how to correctly specify the directory in which I want to save my history detection table as a cvs file, this are the arguments of my function and I get this error:
DetHist_rf <- detectionHistory(recordTable = Spp_RT,
+                  species = "Pan_on",
+                  camOp = camop_problem,
+                  output = c("binary", "count"),
+                  stationCol = "station",
+                  speciesCol = "Short_sp",
+                  recordDateTimeCol = "date_time",
+                  recordDateTimeFormat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
+                  occasionLength = 7,
+                  occasionStartTime = 6,
+                  day1 = "station",
+                  includeEffort = TRUE,
+                  scaleEffort = FALSE,
+                  datesAsOccasionNames = FALSE,
+                  timeZone = "America/Mexico_City",
+                  writecsv = TRUE,
+                  outDir = "//C:/Users/NZLR/Documents/CARLOS/ultima base"
+ )
Error in detectionHistory(recordTable = Spp_RT, species = "Pan_on", camOp = camop_problem,  : 
  outDir does not exist

Thank you,
Nubia

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Detection History, "out dir" argument
parts:
Hi Nubia,
try 
outDir = "C:/Users/NZLR/Documents/CARLOS/ultima base"

Those two forward slashes in the beginning of the argument should not be there.
You can always see if the folder exists by running:

dir.exists("C:/Users/NZLR/Documents/CARLOS/ultima base")

Or simply copy the folder name (in your example:  C:/Users/NZLR/Documents/CARLOS/ultima base) to the address bar of your windows file explorer.

Reversely, to specify the argument correctly, you can open the desired folder in Windows file explorer and copy the folder name from the adress field and paste it as outDir argument (with quotation marks)

Best regards,
Jürgen
